description: walkr4-1 — authored through the bareloop panel (green, js)

jobLines.text: Fix the bug in src/sum.js so the tests in test/sum.test.js pass

goal: Make the tests in test/sum.test.js pass under npm test with 2/2 tests passed, with package.json dependencies unchanged and only files under src/ changed.

notes: No typecheck stage is composed: the survey found no tsconfig/jsconfig, no typescript/tsc dependency and no lint/typecheck script, so the genre's typecheck and typecheck-outside stages are absent by design, not skipped as passing.

The 'no new dependencies' rule is measured as a count of dependency entries across dependencies/devDependencies/peerDependencies/optionalDependencies in package.json, computed by a one-liner passed to node and required to be not-worse than the seed's own count. There is no lockfile in the repo, so package.json is the only dependency surface; the survey says dependencies are currently empty, but the stage reads the seed number rather than a typed zero.

The test stages pass `-- --test-reporter=tap` so the summary is the TAP shape the genre's node-test patterns are measured against (the facts object flags that no reporter is pinned and an inherited NODE_OPTIONS could change the shape); NODE_OPTIONS is set to empty for the same reason. The facts object also says the script hard-pins test/sum.test.js, so extra args after `--` are forwarded to node --test — if this npm version does not forward them the run would still print a spec-reporter summary and the count stages would stop as an unreadable instrument rather than silently pass.

tests-kept counts EXECUTED tests (^# tests N) with a seed floor, so a fix that deletes or skips assertions cannot satisfy the close; suite-no-failures requires the reported fail count to be 0 and, per the genre, a run that never prints the line is treated as unknown; suite-green is the separate exit-code assertion. These are three distinct populations: executed count, failing count, process exit.

Not machine-checked, as the confirmed plan itself says: whether the fix in src/sum.js is correct beyond the two assertions the existing tests make (the doc-comment says 'Sum of a list of numbers', but inputs outside the tests — negatives, non-integers, non-array iterables — are unverified). A behavioural check on unseen inputs would need new tests, which line 1's 'no new dependencies' and the write fence (src/ only) do not obviously invite, so nothing is claimed about it.
Not machine-checked: the issues at https://github.com/hamr0/hol-guard/issues — the job lines never say what to do with them and no stage here reads GitHub.

src/sum.js and test/sum.test.js are the only files that exist at the seed; I invented no other path. package.json was named in the facts object's scripts.test but is not in the seed file listing's [sourcePaths]/[testPaths] blocks — it is used only as a read target of the dependency stage and a write-fence target that the write fence already denies.
